ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Given the figure, the graphs of the linear functions $y_{1}=kx+4$ and $y_{2}=x+m$ intersect at point $P\left(1, 3\right)$. What is the solution set of the inequality $kx+4<x+m$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $x>1$, the graph of the function $y_1=kx+4$ lies entirely below the graph of the function $y_2=x+m$, \\
$\therefore$ the solution set of the inequality $kx+4<x+m$ with respect to $x$ is $x>1$, \\
thus, the answer is: $\boxed{x>1}$.

Since P(1,3) lies on y1=kx+4, substitute to get 3=k+4, so k=-1. Since P(1,3) lies on y2=x+m, substitute to get 3=1+m, so m=2. The inequality becomes -x+4<x+2. Solving gives 2<2x, hence x>1.
method.CoT_raw:

把 k 和 m 代入不等式 kx + 4 < x + m，得到 -x + 4 < x + 2。移项得 2 < 2x，因此 x > 1。

所以该不等式的解集为 x > 1。
